title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
body:
Not a reproducible bug report — a signal from population data that may point at one, and I can't tell from the outside whether the cause is Streamlit or the Hugging Face runtime image.

I enumerated the complete public Hugging Face Spaces catalogue (1,458,692 Spaces) using the `runtime.stage` field HF exposes, and split permanent failures by SDK and creation year.

**`BUILD_ERROR` is falling for every SDK — that part looks healthy.** But `RUNTIME_ERROR` diverges sharply for Streamlit in the 2026 cohort:

| SDK | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **streamlit** | 18.1% | **12.4%** | **31.7%** |
| gradio | 47.1% | 27.0% | 20.8% |
| docker | 31.6% | 19.5% | 20.5% |

Gradio and Docker fell or stayed flat over the same period. Streamlit's rate went from 12.4% to 31.7%.

The failure mode also inverted. Among broken Streamlit Spaces created in 2025: 7,991 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 4,582 `RUNTIME_ERROR`. In 2026: **653 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 5,614 `RUNTIME_ERROR`.** Builds started succeeding and apps started crashing instead.

**Checks I ran before posting, because the obvious explanations would each invalidate this:**

- *Bulk uploaders?* No. The top-10 authors account for 2.3% of the 2026 Streamlit cohort, and excluding them entirely moves the rate from 36.6% to 37.1%. It is spread across 12,432 distinct authors.
- *Just young Spaces still settling?* Newer cohorts are consistently *less* broken across every SDK, so a worse young cohort runs against the trend rather than with it. Separately, 300 error-state Spaces re-queried individually with retries were 300/300 still broken with none recovered, so these are not transient.
- *An age artifact?* Age-standardising Streamlit to Gradio's creation-year distribution moves it 43.50% → 41.16%, so the cohort effect here isn't age composition.

**What I can't determine from outside:** whether this is a Streamlit change, a change in the Streamlit runtime image HF builds, or an interaction between the two. HF controls the Space container, so it may not be yours at all — I've filed the general Spaces census with them separately at huggingface/hub-docs#2743.

If it is useful, I can produce the list of affected Space IDs so someone can look at actual tracebacks, which is the thing this analysis can't reach.

Data (1.46M rows, one row per Space): https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ashsinha1/hf-spaces-census
Method and code: https://github.com/ashishsinha1602/dataset-integrity-audit

comments.body:
This is a population-level reliability signal from Hugging Face Spaces, not a single-app repro. Streamlit’s 2026 cohort inverted from mostly `BUILD_ERROR` to mostly `RUNTIME_ERROR` (12.4% → 31.7%) while Gradio and Docker improved, which is consistent with installs succeeding and the process then failing to stay healthy. The two Streamlit-side events that line up with that pattern are the 1.57 Tornado→Starlette/Uvicorn cutover (May 2026) and the Aug 2026 Starlette 1.4.0 `GZipResponder` startup crash, where pip resolved a compatible-looking stack that then died before serving. Hugging Face also deprecated the built-in Streamlit SDK on 2025-04-30 in favor of a Docker template (port 8501 vs 7860, `/_stcore/health`), so this may be an HF image/proxy interaction rather than a Streamlit regression. Tracebacks or a sample of affected Space IDs are needed before treating any of those as confirmed.

### Related Issues

- [#16341](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16341) — Hosted installs resolved Starlette 1.4.0 and crashed at startup with `GZipResponder.__init__()` (`TypeError`). Same build-ok / runtime-crash shape; the census snapshot (28 Aug 2026) is close to that incident.
- [#15378](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15378) — After 1.57, WebSocket connections fail behind proxies / non-local hosts while the process still starts. HF Spaces fronts apps with a reverse proxy, so a subset of `RUNTIME_ERROR` could be the platform marking apps that never become ready.
- [#7076](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7076) — `/_stcore/health` misbehavior in Docker/cloud deployments. HF Streamlit Docker templates typically health-check that endpoint; a 503 or parse failure can surface as `RUNTIME_ERROR` after a successful build.

No duplicate of this census itself was found. The reporter’s companion write-up is [huggingface/hub-docs#2743](https://github.com/huggingface/hub-docs/issues/2743).

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

The triage comment prompted me to re-cut the data by **creation month** instead of year, and that changes the picture in a way that seems worth having on the record: the elevated `RUNTIME_ERROR` rate is a **bounded window, and it does not line up with either candidate cause suggested above.**

`RUNTIME_ERROR` share of Streamlit Spaces, by month created:

| Created | n | RUNTIME_ERROR | BUILD_ERROR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-08 | 1,757 | 13.9% | 5.7% |
| 2025-09 | 1,905 | 14.3% | 5.0% |
| 2025-10 | 1,570 | 11.5% | 4.5% |
| **2025-11** | 1,791 | **30.9%** | 6.8% |
| 2025-12 | 1,744 | 35.8% | 4.9% |
| 2026-01 | 2,128 | 45.3% | 4.4% |
| **2026-02** | 2,003 | **48.8%** | 3.6% |
| 2026-03 | 2,307 | 46.4% | 5.8% |
| 2026-04 | 3,797 | 40.4% | 3.4% |
| 2026-05 | 3,175 | 24.9% | 3.4% |
| 2026-06 | 2,787 | 8.6% | 3.5% |
| 2026-07 | 1,065 | 3.2% | 1.7% |

The window opens between **October and November 2025** (11.5% → 30.9%), peaks in **Jan–Feb 2026** at ~48%, and is back to baseline by June 2026.

**Against the two suggested causes:**
- The 1.57 Tornado→Starlette cutover (May 2026) is *five months after* the window opens, and by May 2026 the rate is already falling.
- The Starlette 1.4.0 `GZipResponder` crash (Aug 2026, #16341) is *after* the window closes.

Neither timing fits. Whatever this was appears to have started around Nov 2025 and been resolved around May–June 2026.

**The caveat that cuts the other way, stated plainly:** this is a single snapshot (28 Aug 2026) bucketed by creation date, so the falling tail is confounded — Spaces created in June–August 2026 are only weeks old and may simply not have had time to break. I would not read the decline as recovery on this evidence alone.

**The rise, however, is not an age artifact, and that is the load-bearing part.** Spaces created 2025-06 to 2025-10 are *older* than those created 2026-01 to 2026-04, yet break at 8.6–14.3% against 40–49%. Breakage otherwise rises monotonically with age across every SDK in this dataset, so an older cohort failing three to four times *less* runs against the trend rather than with it.

**One thing the triage comment got exactly right** — I can confirm the SDK deprecation from the volume data. Streamlit Space creation drops from **7,317 in April 2025 to 1,783 in May 2025**, a 4x fall in one month, matching the 2025-04-30 date. `BUILD_ERROR` also falls off a cliff shortly after (31.4% in April 2025 → 5.0% by June), consistent with the Docker-template migration removing a class of install failure.

Happy to supply the affected Space IDs — I have ~5,600 Streamlit Spaces in `RUNTIME_ERROR` created in 2026, and can filter to the Nov 2025 – Apr 2026 window if that is the useful cut. Say which format helps and I will post it.

Full data (1.46M rows, one per Space): https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ashsinha1/hf-spaces-census

**Correction: this is not a Streamlit problem, and I filed it in the wrong place.**

I pulled `runtime.errorMessage` from the Spaces API for samples inside and outside the window. The failures are not application crashes — they are Hugging Face scheduler failures.

| Error class | 2026-01/02 (n=300) | 2025-09/10 (n=295) |
|---|---|---|
| `Scheduling failure: unable to schedule` | **90.0%** | 42.0% |
| Launch timed out (30 min) | 6.3% | 18.6% |
| **App-level crash** (traceback / exit code) | **2.7%** | 27.5% |

Odds ratio 12.4 for the scheduling class. I re-ran it independently on a fresh sample with a different seed (n=60 per group) and got 80.0% vs 28.3% — same direction, same magnitude.

**Decomposing the census by cohort settles it.** Multiplying each cohort's RUNTIME_ERROR rate by the sampled share of each error class:

| Cohort | RUNTIME_ERROR | sched-fail % of cohort | **non-sched RE % of cohort** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-09/10 | 13.0% | 5.5% | **7.6%** |
| 2025-11/12 | 33.4% | 28.1% | **5.3%** |
| 2026-01/02 | 47.0% | 42.3% | **4.7%** |
| 2026-04 | 40.4% | 37.7% | **2.7%** |
| 2026-06 | 8.6% | 1.5% | **7.1%** |

The right-hand column is the point. **Non-scheduling runtime errors are flat-to-declining across the entire window.** Every point of the rise and the whole return to baseline is scheduling failure. App-level crashes — the only class Streamlit code could produce — are *lower* inside the window (1.4% of cohort) than outside it (2.8%).

Supporting: RUNTIME_ERROR displaces SLEEPING almost exactly. `(RE + SLEEPING) / n` holds at 88–92% for every month from 2025-06 to 2026-06 while RE's share of that pair swings 12.6% → 53.1% → 9.7%. These are Spaces that would have been asleep, failing at wake — not apps crashing at startup. `gcTimeout` is 48h for 100% of both groups, so it isn't a sleep-policy difference.

**Your triage was right to reject both proposed causes.** Neither the Tornado→Starlette cutover nor the Starlette 1.4.0 crash fits, and now it's clear why: no Streamlit-side change could produce this, because Streamlit's code is not what's failing.

**One thing I can't explain, stated as open:** why the rate is Streamlit-specific. In the same months, 42.3% of the streamlit cohort hit scheduling failures against 3.6% of gradio — 12x, same platform, same period. So *something* about which Spaces fail to schedule correlates with the SDK even though the failure isn't in Streamlit. I have an untested hypothesis (streamlit skews toward classroom cohorts — 26 of 300 sampled READMEs share one project title, and affected Spaces are 78.7% never-modified-after-day-one vs 63.3% for healthy ones) which would make it a population difference in account tier rather than anything technical. I would not assert that without testing it.

I'm refiling this with Hugging Face, where the scheduler lives. **Please close this** — sorry for the misdirected report, and thanks for the triage that pushed me to look at the actual error strings.

Method and data: https://github.com/ashishsinha1602/dataset-integrity-audit

[USER] Thanks for this analysis! We also did a quick check on our internal error data, and it had been declining significantly over the last couple of months. We also have some internal metrics on this related to hugginface deployed apps, there are higher error rates, but it doesn't look like errors that are specifically related to Streamlit
